newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TEXAS EXPECTED TO ANNOUNCE SIGNING OF WETTELAND.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TEXAS EXPECTED TO ANNOUNCE SIGNING OF WETTELAND.

text.p: The Texas Rangers are expected to announce the signing on Monday of ace reliever John Wetteland, the Most Valuable Player of the New York Yankees World Series' triumph.
The Rangers have scheduled a news conference for 4 p.m. EST (2100 gmt).
According to various reports, the 30-year-old Wetteland agreed to a four-year deal worth between $21 and $23 million with the Rangers.

Wetteland became the first pitcher to save all four wins in a World Series as the Yankees battled back from a 2-0 deficit to sweep the last four games from the Atlanta Braves. He also was the first reliever to win World Series MVP honours since Oakland's Rollie Fingers in 1974.

Wetteland combined with young Panamanian Mariano Rivera to give New York the best bullpen tandem in baseball. Wetteland was 2-3 with a 2.82 ERA in 62 relief appearances, converting 43 of 46 save opportunities.
The loss of Wetteland should move Rivera into the role of closer for the Yankees.
Wetteland would fill a glaring need for the Rangers, who lost inconsistent closer Mike Henneman to free agency. Henneman was 0-7 with 31 saves, but had a 5.79 ERA.
Another member of the Texas bullpen, lefty Mike Stanton, signed as a free agent with the Yankees last week.
